params.prompt: Edit the supplied REAL model-home interior photograph into a photorealistic design proposal. This is an image-to-image architectural restyle, not a new room. Preserve the exact camera, room proportions, all window and door openings, glazing divisions, original ceiling and crown moulding. Crown/Gaithersburg townhouses and nearby roofs outside only. Use bright natural daylight with realistic neutral white balance, soft shadows and credible material textures; no dramatic orange cast. No people, logos, labels, watermark, collage or added text. Design working name Cocoa & Chrome: sophisticated contemporary showroom, warm dark espresso/cocoa-brown wood, cool silver polished chrome details, warm off-white upholstery, restrained blue. All drawer units, sideboards, consoles and bedside cabinets are monolithic floor-standing boxes on flush or deeply recessed continuous plinths. NO little feet, no visible furniture legs under storage, no open frame bases and no floating wall-hung cabinets. Wood is deep chocolate brown with subtle straight grain, not orange or rustic walnut. Chrome is actually SILVER, not brass/gold/bronze; use polished metal selectively, not an all-mirrored room. Floors are natural neutral medium-light oak with a loose oatmeal rug; no wall-to-wall carpet. Keep the room build uncomplicated: smooth beautifully finished painted walls, no ornate wall panels, no costly whole-wall slab or elaborate ceiling interventions. Great room: match the supplied corner view exactly. Keep the centered original fireplace chase and linear insert, both high horizontal transom windows on the fireplace wall, and the existing terrace glazing along the left wall. TV is mounted ABOVE the fireplace (intentional owner change from original); remove the TV from the right-side bay. Place two low closed-front dark cocoa consoles, one on each side below the high windows, with matching thin chrome cabinet pulls and solid continuous plinths down to the floor. Above each console, below its high window, hang sibling abstract artworks in thin silver frames, mostly chalk white with expressive inky/denim-blue brushwork, not identical copies. Keep two very comfortable softly rounded warm-white upholstered chairs in the source's approximate positions with concealed swivel bases. Main sofa is an oversized low white Cloud-style sofa facing the fireplace, photographed from behind/side like the original foreground. Use one substantial dark cocoa oval coffee table on a closed pedestal/plinth and a pale quiet rug. Sculptural polished chrome dome table lamp and polished chrome arc floor lamp, soft light through sheer ivory curtains; one tasteful green plant. Clear usable paths. No yellow curtains from the original, no art covering glazing. PALETTE A: all walls a clearly perceptible soft warm stone/mink-greige paint, ceiling and trim warm white. Wall tone is richer and slightly deeper than the upholstery, so the white sofa and chairs are defined against it. Muted smoky denim and ink blue only in the two white-dominant artworks, three thoughtfully placed blue cushions and a small blue glass object. Crisp silver chrome gives modern highlights against the dark brown storage. Quiet, collected, bright and luxurious. NO yellow accent in this version, no coordinated green cushions. The dark consoles must visibly meet the floor on continuous solid plinths.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: It's a nice design, but it feels like a cheap home.
feedbackLog.priorRecommendation: A for the great room: warm stone walls keep the white furniture soft, chrome provides silver highlights and blue remains easy to adjust. B deliberately tests stronger color; C shows the palette in a bedroom.
feedbackLog.response: Improve material depth, millwork craftsmanship, furniture scale and lighting hierarchy; compare warm mineral stone against smoky ink blue. Retain white upholstery, dark brown floor-standing storage and silver/chrome. Exploratory only.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: I like D better; add a hint of yellow in pillows/small objects or green in plants, and show more rooms.
feedbackLog.interpretation: D is the preferred base. Compare accent treatments in the great room and extend into dining and primary bedroom. Accent palette and new room designs remain pending feedback.

feedbackLog.userFeedback: Mineral & Walnut feels better and seems suitable as a foundation for Christmas and Halloween decorating; requests designer assessment of the new design.
feedbackLog.interpretation: User currently leans toward Mineral & Walnut overall. D remains the preferred version within Option 2. This is consultation, not authorization to replace designs, expand renders or deploy changes.
